# PART 8: HOME CARDIO

## Cardio Options

**Option 1: Brisk walking (the foundation)**
- Build daily steps by about 1,000 per fortnight from his baseline until he reaches 8,000–10,000 per day.
- Dedicated walks of 30–45 min at a conversational but breathing-noticeably pace.
- Stair climbing in his building is excellent. Walk up, take the lift or walk slowly down to spare his knees.

**Option 2: Indoor Zone 2 circuit (20–30 min)**
60 seconds each, continuous, at conversational pace:
1. High march in place
2. Shadow boxing
3. Alternating step-back lunges (slow)
4. Lateral shuffle steps
5. Standing knee-to-elbow crunch, alternating
6. Bodyweight good morning to calf raise

If he's gasping, slow down rather than stopping.

**Option 3: Quiet intervals (hard)**
Pick 4 and rotate through them:
- Step-back burpee (no jump)
- Slow mountain climbers
- Bear crawl
- Fast shadow boxing (feet planted)
- Speed skaters with no jump (wide lateral step and reach)
- Plank to downward dog shoulder taps

**Interval session structure:** 5 min warm-up march and shadow boxing, main set, 5 min easy cool-down with hip flexor and calf stretches.

**Cardio safety:**
- If knees ache, swap lunges and skaters for marching and shadow boxing.
- After heavy push days, choose standing interval exercises to spare wrists and shoulders.
- Use the mat for hands-down work and trainers on hard floors.
- **Chest pain, dizziness, unusual breathlessness or palpitations:** stop immediately and seek medical advice.
- Drink an extra ~500 ml of water per 30–45 min of sweaty cardio.
- **If strength stalls or he feels run down, cut intervals first.**

# PART 9: SATURDAY GAME DAY

**Purpose:** A short, fun session for motivation, skill-building and work capacity, designed not to eat into recovery.

## Ground Rules
1. 25–35 minutes, including warm-up.
2. Never to failure. RPE 6–7 in Phase 1, **RPE 7 firmly** in Phases 2–3.
3. No Nordics, no max chin-up work, no pistols to failure.
4. Maximum 3–4 short hangs or knee raises, since his grip took heavy work on Friday.
5. No jumping. Everything fits on or around the mat.
6. In Phase 2, push-up variations are two rungs easier than his Session A variation. Swap lunges for regular squats if his legs are heavily fatigued.
7. If he hates a format, drop it.

## Session Structure
1. **Warm-up (5 min):** march, shadow boxing, cat-cow, world's greatest stretch, 10 squats.
2. **Skill play (8–10 min):** 1–2 skills from the menu, in short fresh attempts.
3. **The game (12–20 min).**
4. **Cool-down (5–6 min):** the standard post-session cool-down.

## Skill Menu

| Skill | Progression |
|---|---|
| Crow pose | Toes-on-floor lean → one foot lifted → full crow hold, building to 10–20 sec |
| Handstand | Wall walk to 45° → chest-to-wall hold → heel pulls off the wall (only if pike push-ups are solid) |
| L-sit | Tuck sit with hands on books → one leg extended → full L-sit |
| Shrimp squat balance | Door frame support → fingertip support → unsupported |
| Deep squat hold | Accumulate 2–3 minutes |
| Skin the cat (Phase 3 only) | Only if pain-free, bar very secure, and he has 5+ chin-ups |

He logs his best hold or cleanest attempt each week.

## Game Formats

**Deck of Cards.** Suit is the movement, card value is the reps (J/Q/K = 10, Ace = 11, Joker = 30-sec plank).
- ♥ Push-ups
- ♠ Squats or step-back lunges
- ♦ Glute bridges (single- or double-leg)
- ♣ Dead bugs (per side) or shadow boxing (value × 3 punches)

Half a deck in Phase 1, up to three-quarters in Phase 2. 20-minute cap. Record how far he gets.

**Dice Roulette.** First die picks the exercise; second die sets the reps. Play for 15 min and count total rolls.

| First die | Exercise | Second die × |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Push-ups | × 2 |
| 2 | Squats | × 3 |
| 3 | Slow mountain climbers (per side) | × 2 |
| 4 | Glute bridges | × 3 |
| 5 | Bear crawl (mat lengths) | × 1 |
| 6 | Wild card: 20 sec plank, 20 sec hollow hold, or 30 sec fast shadow boxing | — |

**Fight Night.** 6 × 2-minute shadow boxing rounds with 1 minute in the "corner": 5 push-ups and 10 squats, then rest for the remainder. A boxing timer app with bells helps.

**Ladder Race.** 1 push-up and 2 squats, then 2 and 4, then 3 and 6, and so on. 12-minute cap. Score is the highest clean rung.

**Animal Flow Circuit.** Bear crawl, crab walk, slow lizard crawl, ape walk side-to-side, beast-to-crab transitions. 40 sec on, 20 sec off, 2–3 rounds.

**Trainer's Challenge.** You set a mystery challenge on Friday evening (e.g., 100 push-ups in as few sets as possible, or 3 minutes of accumulated hollow hold). He films it, and you keep a leaderboard of his past attempts.

## Boss Battle (Weeks 3, 7 and 10)
Fastest time for 3 rounds of:
- 10 push-ups (scale to knee push-ups if needed and note it)
- 20 squats
- 10 glute bridges
- 30-second plank
- 10 slow mountain climbers per side

He beats the boss with a faster time at the same or harder scaling. Film it.

## Game Day Autoregulation
- **Skill play plus one easy round only** if Friday left him very sore, he slept under 6 hours, or his Monday performance dropped the previous week.
- **Skip it entirely** if he shows overreaching signs or has any joint pain.
- **Red flag:** If Monday sessions are consistently weaker since adding Game Day, halve the game portion or switch to skill play only. The main programme takes priority.

# PART 10: MOBILITY

## Daily Primer (8–10 min, Every Day)
1. **Cat-cow:** 8 slow reps
2. **Wrist prep series** (on hands and knees):
   - Fingers forward, rock gently: 10
   - Fingers back towards knees, rock gently: 10
   - Palm-up flips, light rocks: 8
   - Wrist circles: 10 each direction
3. **Thread the needle:** 6 per side, 2-sec pause at end range
4. **Kneeling hip flexor stretch** (glute squeezed, pelvis tucked): 30 sec per side
5. **Half-kneeling ankle rocks:** 10 per side, heel down
6. **Deep squat hold:** 60 sec, holding the door frame if needed
7. **Dead hang:** 20–30 sec, relaxed

**Short on time:** steps 2, 5 and 6 only.

**Frequency:** 5+ days per week in Phase 1, every day in Phases 2–3.

## Sunday Mobility Flow (25–30 min)

**Block 1: Breathe and loosen (5 min)**
- 90/90 breathing (on back, feet on the sofa): 2 min, long exhales
- Cat-cow: 10
- Quadruped thoracic rotation: 8 per side

**Block 2: Hips (8 min)**
- 90/90 hip switches: 10 total

- Pancake fold: 60 sec
- Seated pike fold: 60 sec

- Deep squat with rotation: 5 per side, then 60 sec still hold

**Block 4: Shoulders and upper back (7 min)**
- Towel dislocates: 10 slow, narrowing the grip slightly each week
- Wall slides: 10

# Complete 12-Week Bodyweight Strength Programme
**Client:** Male, 27, beginner | **Setting:** Small flat, noise-sensitive | **Equipment:** Yoga mat, doorway pull-up bar, household items (sturdy chair, sofa or bed, towel, books, wall)

This is the master document with every adjustment included: the original strength plan, nutrition, home cardio, the high-intensity Phase 2, Saturday Game Day, mobility, and equipment guidance. Where earlier versions conflicted, this document takes precedence.

---

# PART 1: SETUP AND PRINCIPLES

## Pre-Programme Checklist (Video Call Before Week 1)

**Pull-up bar safety.** Have him show you the bar on camera and confirm:
- The door frame is solid wood or masonry, not a hollow architrave.
- The bar is rated well above his bodyweight.
- He has tested it with a controlled hang before any dynamic work.

Cantilever bars resist downward force but can lift out if pulled outward. **No leaning-back rows on the doorway bar.** He should check the bar before every session.

**Household items:**
- A sturdy, non-wheeled chair or sofa edge for elevated split squats, dips and pistols to box.
- A bed or heavy sofa to anchor his heels for Nordic curls.
- A towel on a smooth floor for sliding leg curls and shoulder dislocates.
- Books for deficit push-ups and elevated pike push-ups.

**Noise:** No jumping or plyometrics anywhere in the programme. This covers strength sessions, cardio and Game Day.

**Information to collect for nutrition:**
- Bodyweight (7-day morning average) and height
- Primary goal: lean gain, recomposition or fat loss
- 3-day food log including one weekend day
- Dietary restrictions, allergies, dislikes
- Cooking setup (fridge, freezer and hob space)
- Medical history. If he has a diagnosed condition, a history of disordered eating, or medications that affect appetite or weight, refer him to a registered dietitian or GP.
- Current average daily steps (7 days from his phone)

**Progress photos:** Front, side and back in consistent lighting at Weeks 0, 4, 8 and 12.

**Filming:** One working set of every new exercise the first time he does it, plus all assessment and retest sessions in full.

**Logging:** Every set, with reps and RPE (1–10, where 10 is failure).

## Training Principles

**Frequency:** Three full-body strength sessions (Mon/Wed/Fri), 45–60 minutes each, plus a short Saturday Game Day.

**Double progression:** Each exercise has a rep range. When he hits the top of the range on all sets with clean form at the target RPE, he moves up one rung next session. If he can't reach the bottom of the range, he drops one rung.
- Phase 1 trigger: top of range at RPE 8 or below
- Phase 2 trigger: top of range at RPE 8.5
- Phase 3: hardest variation he can manage for the target reps

**Tempo notation:** eccentric–pause–concentric–pause. So 3-1-1-0 means 3 seconds down, 1-second pause, 1 second up, no pause at the top. Enforce tempo, because it's a primary loading tool.

**Rest:**
- Main lifts: 90–120 sec in Phase 1, 2–3 min in Phases 2–3
- Accessories and core: 60 sec

**Intensity guide (used for all training):**

| Zone | Talk test | RPE |
|---|---|---|
| Easy (Zone 2) | Full sentences, slightly breathy | 3–4 |
| Moderate | Short phrases | 5–6 |
| Hard | A few words at most | 7–8 |
| Near-max strength set | 1–2 reps left in the tank | 8–9 |

For cardio, his estimated max heart rate is about 193 bpm. Zone 2 is roughly 115–135 bpm, but the talk test is more reliable for him.

---

# PART 2: PROGRESSION LADDERS

**Horizontal push**
1. Incline push-up (hands on sofa or chair)
2. Knee push-up
3. Full push-up
4. Tempo push-up (3-1-1-0)
5. Deficit push-up (hands on books)
6. Archer push-up negatives → archer push-up
7. Pseudo-planche push-up

**Vertical push**
1. Pike push-up on floor
2. Feet-elevated pike push-up (feet on chair)
3. Deep feet-elevated pike push-up (hands on books)
4. Wall-supported handstand hold → wall handstand negatives

**Vertical pull**
1. Dead hang and scapular pulls
2. Flexed-arm hang (chin over bar)
3. Chin-up negatives (5-second lower)
4. Partial chin-ups plus negatives (cluster sets)
5. Full chin-ups
6. Pull-ups (overhand)
7. Tempo or paused pull-ups

**Horizontal pull**
1. Door-frame row (grip both sides of an open door frame, lean back, row)
2. Single-arm door-frame row
3. Table row, only with a genuinely solid table
- **If he buys rings:** ring rows replace door-frame rows from Phase 2 onwards. Progress by walking the feet forward, elevating the feet, then going single-arm.

**Squat pattern**
1. Bodyweight squat (tempo)
2. Split squat
3. Rear-foot-elevated split squat (RFESS, back foot on sofa or chair)
4. Tempo RFESS
5. Assisted shrimp squat or assisted pistol (holding the door frame)
6. Pistol to chair, lowering the box height over time
7. Full shrimp squat or pistol

**Hinge and posterior chain**
1. Glute bridge
2. Single-leg glute bridge
3. Single-leg hip thrust (shoulders on sofa)
4. Single-leg RDL (bodyweight, slow)
5. Sliding leg curl (towel, both legs)
6. Single-leg sliding leg curl
7. Nordic curl negatives (heels anchored, hands catch on the mat)

**Dips**
1. Bench dip on chair, knees bent
2. Bench dip, legs straight
3. Feet-elevated bench dip
- Drop dips entirely if there's any front-of-shoulder pain and replace them with an extra set of push-ups.

**Core**
- Plank → hollow body hold → hollow rocks
- Side plank → side plank with top-leg raise
- Hanging knee raise → hanging leg raise
- Dead bug, bird dog

---

# PART 3: WEEKLY STRUCTURE

## Master Weekly Template

| Day | Strength | Cardio | Mobility |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Mon** | Session A | Daily steps | Primer, warm-up add-on, cool-down |
| **Tue** | — | Zone 2 (Phases 1–2) / Intervals (Phase 3) | Primer |
| **Wed** | Session B | Daily steps | Primer, warm-up add-on, cool-down |
| **Thu** | — | Intervals (Week 5 only) / Zone 2 / rest | Primer |
| **Fri** | Session A or C | Daily steps | Primer, warm-up add-on, cool-down |
| **Sat** | **Game Day** (25–35 min) | Optional 15–20 min easy walk | Primer, cool-down |
| **Sun** | Rest | Optional long easy walk | **Sunday Mobility Flow** (25–30 min) |

**Key scheduling rules:**
- No hard cardio the day before a heavy strength session.
- No hard intervals directly after strength work. An easy 5–10 minute walk afterwards is fine.
- At least one day a week with no structured training beyond mobility and walking. Sunday serves this role.

## Standard Strength Warm-Up (Every Session, About 8 Minutes)
1. Arm circles and towel shoulder dislocates: 10 each
2. Cat-cow: 10
3. World's greatest stretch: 5 per side
4. Bodyweight squats: 10
5. Glute bridges: 10
6. Scapular push-ups: 10
7. Dead hang: 20 seconds
8. One easy set of the first exercise

**Then add the session-specific mobility add-on (3–4 min):**

| Session | Add-on |
|---|---|
| **A** | Wrist prep series (5 reps per position), gentle couch stretch 30 sec per side, push-up plus × 10 |
| **B** | Wall slides × 10, 5 extra slow towel dislocates, half-kneeling ankle rocks × 10 per side, active hang with scapular pulls × 5 |
| **C** | Leg swings front-to-back and side-to-side × 10 each per leg, ankle rocks × 10 per side, inchworm walkouts × 5, slow single-leg RDL reach × 5 per leg |

Warm-up mobility is dynamic only. Save long static holds for afterwards.

## Post-Session Cool-Down (After Strength and Game Day, 5–6 Minutes)
1. Child's pose with side reach: 30 sec centre, 20 sec each side
2. Doorway chest stretch: 30 sec per side
3. Supine towel hamstring stretch: 30 sec per side (gentle after Nordic sessions)
4. Figure-4 glute stretch: 30 sec per side
5. Couch or kneeling hip flexor stretch: 30 sec per side
6. Wrist flexor and extensor stretches: 20 sec each, each hand

---

# PART 4: WEEK 1 ASSESSMENT

## Strength Baseline (Monday, Filmed)
- Max strict push-ups (chest to fist height, no sagging hips)
- Max chin-ups. If zero, max flexed-arm hang time.
- Max dead hang time
- Max bodyweight squats at 2-0-1-0 tempo, stopping at form breakdown

- Plank hold time
- Hollow body hold time

## Mobility Screen (Same Call, Filmed From the Side)
1. **Knee-to-wall:** furthest toe-to-wall distance with knee touching and heel down. Under 8 cm is restricted; 10 cm or more is good.
2. **Deep squat hold:** 30 sec, heels down. Note heel lift, rounding or knee collapse.
3. **Toe touch:** straight legs, fingertip distance from the floor.
4. **Overhead wall test:** back, head and bottom on the wall, straight arms overhead. Do thumbs reach the wall without the lower back arching?
5. **Wrist extension:** on hands and knees, can he comfortably shift his shoulders past his wrists?
6. **Couch stretch:** can he stay upright with the torso vertical?

## Cardio Baseline (Tuesday)
**1-mile brisk walk test** on flat ground, timed. If he can't get outside, use a **5-minute step-back burpee test** at a sustainable pace, counting total reps.

## Step Baseline
Seven days of step data recorded during Week 1.

# PART 6: PHASE 2 — HIGH-INTENSITY BUILD (WEEKS 5–8)

**Goal:** Harder variations, lower reps, and intensity techniques to create overload without external weight.
**Effort:** RPE 8–9 on main lifts, RPE 8 on accessories.
**Rest:** 2–3 min on main lifts.
**Rule:** If he can do more than 8 clean reps of a main-lift variation, move him up the ladder even if reps drop to 4.
**Session order:** A, B, C every week. Session C starts in Week 5.
**Rings:** If he's bought them, ring rows replace door-frame rows from this phase.

## Intensity Techniques (Final Set Only, Never Every Set)
Brief him on video before Week 5.

- **Rest-pause:** Set to RPE 9, rest 15 sec, more clean reps, rest 15 sec, repeat once. Count the total.
- **Mechanical drop set:** Set to RPE 9 on a hard variation, then switch straight to an easier one and continue to RPE 9. Example: deficit → full → knee push-ups.
- **Iso-hold finisher:** After the last rep, hold the hardest position as long as possible.
- **1.5 reps:** All the way down, halfway up, back down, all the way up. That counts as one rep.
- **Cluster sets:** One hard set broken into mini-sets with 20-sec rests. Example: 3 chin-ups, rest, 2, rest, 2.
- **Eccentric overload:** Use assistance (a chair, or the other leg) to reach the hard position, then lower slowly unaided.

### Session A: Push Strength
1. **Push-up, hardest variation for 4–8 reps** (deficit, tempo 3-1-1-0, or archer negatives): 4 × 4–8, RPE 8–9
   - Last set: mechanical drop set
2. **Chin-ups:** 5 × 2–5 full reps, RPE 8–9
   - Fewer than 2 full reps: cluster sets of partials plus negatives, 8–10 total reps per set
3. **RFESS:** 4 × 6–8 per leg, tempo 3-1-1-0
   - Last set: 1.5 reps, 5 per leg
4. **Single-leg hip thrust** (shoulders on sofa): 3 × 8–12 per leg, 2-sec squeeze at top
5. **Bench dip** (legs straight or feet elevated): 3 × 6–10
   - Last set: iso-hold at 90° elbow bend
6. **Hollow body hold:** 4 × 20–30 sec

### Session B: Pull Strength
1. **Feet-elevated pike push-up:** 4 × 4–8, RPE 8–9, tempo 3-0-1-0
2. **Single-arm door-frame row** (or feet-elevated ring row): 4 × 6–10 per arm, 2-sec squeeze
   - Last set: rest-pause
3. **Chin-up eccentric overload:** 4 × 3. Step up from a chair to the top position, then lower over 8 seconds.
4. **Assisted shrimp squat or assisted pistol to chair:** 4 × 5–8 per leg
5. **Single-leg sliding leg curl:** 3 × 6–8 per leg
6. **Hanging knee raise → hanging leg raise:** 3 × 6–12, no swinging, 1-sec pause at top

### Session C: Unilateral and Posterior Chain
1. **Archer push-up** (or archer negatives): 4 × 3–6 per side
2. **Flexed-arm hang:** 3 × max, finishing each with a slow negative
3. **Pistol to chair:** 4 × 4–6 per leg, 3-sec lower. Lower the box height as he progresses.
4. **Single-leg RDL:** 3 × 8 per leg, 4-sec lower, 2-sec pause at the bottom
5. **Nordic curl negatives:** 3 × 3–5, fighting the descent as long as possible
6. **Side plank with top-leg raise:** 3 × 20–30 sec per side

## Phase 2 Autoregulation and Stop Rules

**Reduce the session (no techniques, cap at RPE 7) if:**
- Reps drop by 2 or more on a main lift versus last session.
- He slept under 6 hours the night before.
- Soreness from the previous session still limits movement.

**Regress the exercise one rung for a week if:**
- Pain on the inside of the elbow (chin-up volume) or front of the shoulder (dips, pike push-ups).
- Knee pain during pistols or shrimp squats.

**Bring the deload forward a week** if overreaching signs persist across a full week: ongoing fatigue, falling performance, irritability, poor sleep, or elevated resting heart rate.

# PART 8: HOME CARDIO

## Cardio Options

**Option 1: Brisk walking (the foundation)**
- Build daily steps by about 1,000 per fortnight from his baseline until he reaches 8,000–10,000 per day.
- Dedicated walks of 30–45 min at a conversational but breathing-noticeably pace.
- Stair climbing in his building is excellent. Walk up, take the lift or walk slowly down to spare his knees.

**Option 2: Indoor Zone 2 circuit (20–30 min)**
60 seconds each, continuous, at conversational pace:
1. High march in place
2. Shadow boxing
3. Alternating step-back lunges (slow)
4. Lateral shuffle steps
5. Standing knee-to-elbow crunch, alternating
6. Bodyweight good morning to calf raise

If he's gasping, slow down rather than stopping.

**Option 3: Quiet intervals (hard)**
Pick 4 and rotate through them:
- Step-back burpee (no jump)
- Slow mountain climbers
- Bear crawl
- Fast shadow boxing (feet planted)
- Speed skaters with no jump (wide lateral step and reach)
- Plank to downward dog shoulder taps

# PART 9: SATURDAY GAME DAY

**Purpose:** A short, fun session for motivation, skill-building and work capacity, designed not to eat into recovery.

## Ground Rules
1. 25–35 minutes, including warm-up.
2. Never to failure. RPE 6–7 in Phase 1, **RPE 7 firmly** in Phases 2–3.
3. No Nordics, no max chin-up work, no pistols to failure.
4. Maximum 3–4 short hangs or knee raises, since his grip took heavy work on Friday.
5. No jumping. Everything fits on or around the mat.
6. In Phase 2, push-up variations are two rungs easier than his Session A variation. Swap lunges for regular squats if his legs are heavily fatigued.
7. If he hates a format, drop it.

## Session Structure
1. **Warm-up (5 min):** march, shadow boxing, cat-cow, world's greatest stretch, 10 squats.
2. **Skill play (8–10 min):** 1–2 skills from the menu, in short fresh attempts.
3. **The game (12–20 min).**
4. **Cool-down (5–6 min):** the standard post-session cool-down.

## Skill Menu

| Skill | Progression |
|---|---|
| Crow pose | Toes-on-floor lean → one foot lifted → full crow hold, building to 10–20 sec |
| Handstand | Wall walk to 45° → chest-to-wall hold → heel pulls off the wall (only if pike push-ups are solid) |
| L-sit | Tuck sit with hands on books → one leg extended → full L-sit |
| Shrimp squat balance | Door frame support → fingertip support → unsupported |
| Deep squat hold | Accumulate 2–3 minutes |
| Skin the cat (Phase 3 only) | Only if pain-free, bar very secure, and he has 5+ chin-ups |

He logs his best hold or cleanest attempt each week.

## Game Formats

**Deck of Cards.** Suit is the movement, card value is the reps (J/Q/K = 10, Ace = 11, Joker = 30-sec plank).
- ♥ Push-ups
- ♠ Squats or step-back lunges
- ♦ Glute bridges (single- or double-leg)
- ♣ Dead bugs (per side) or shadow boxing (value × 3 punches)

Half a deck in Phase 1, up to three-quarters in Phase 2. 20-minute cap. Record how far he gets.

**Dice Roulette.** First die picks the exercise; second die sets the reps. Play for 15 min and count total rolls.

| First die | Exercise | Second die × |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Push-ups | × 2 |
| 2 | Squats | × 3 |
| 3 | Slow mountain climbers (per side) | × 2 |
| 4 | Glute bridges | × 3 |
| 5 | Bear crawl (mat lengths) | × 1 |
| 6 | Wild card: 20 sec plank, 20 sec hollow hold, or 30 sec fast shadow boxing | — |

**Fight Night.** 6 × 2-minute shadow boxing rounds with 1 minute in the "corner": 5 push-ups and 10 squats, then rest for the remainder. A boxing timer app with bells helps.

**Ladder Race.** 1 push-up and 2 squats, then 2 and 4, then 3 and 6, and so on. 12-minute cap. Score is the highest clean rung.

**Animal Flow Circuit.** Bear crawl, crab walk, slow lizard crawl, ape walk side-to-side, beast-to-crab transitions. 40 sec on, 20 sec off, 2–3 rounds.

**Trainer's Challenge.** You set a mystery challenge on Friday evening (e.g., 100 push-ups in as few sets as possible, or 3 minutes of accumulated hollow hold). He films it, and you keep a leaderboard of his past attempts.

## Boss Battle (Weeks 3, 7 and 10)
Fastest time for 3 rounds of:
- 10 push-ups (scale to knee push-ups if needed and note it)
- 20 squats
- 10 glute bridges
- 30-second plank
- 10 slow mountain climbers per side

He beats the boss with a faster time at the same or harder scaling. Film it.
